subject: Deckridge: request latency accumulation & backpressure symptoms
messages:
From: ops@deckridge.com
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: URGENT: Request latency accumulation & elevated 502s — Deckridge production

Hi Rachel,

We’re seeing an escalating production issue since ~08:45 PDT. Symptoms: p95 is roughly unchanged but p99 and p999 are climbing rapidly, queue depth on our request path is growing, and we’re seeing intermittent 502s that correlate with bursts. Throughput to the Redwood endpoint has dropped ~18% during the highest tail periods.

Quick facts:
- Region: us-west-2
- Error rate: baseline 0.08% -> spike 1.9% (502/524-ish)
- Token throughput down ~18% across our 4k request pool
- Queue depth (our side) increased from median 6 -> 38 in the last 30m

We suspect some form of backpressure or concurrency capping on your side causing request pileups; alternatively this could be a model or kernel-level stall (KV cache thrash). We’ve attached a small set of client-side logs and a screenshot of our request queue.

Can you triage immediately? We’re ready to jump on a bridge — Deckridge SRE team is standing by. This is impacting checkout flows for customers.

Attachments: deckridge_latency_logs_20281005.zip, pipeline_snapshot_09h10.png

— ops@deckridge.com
Deckridge SRE
From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: ops@deckridge.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-05T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Request latency accumulation & elevated 502s — Deckridge production

Hi — thanks for the quick flag. I’ve copied our on-call SRE and platform lead. We’re pulling telemetry now. Proposed immediate steps:

- Stand up a short bridge (15–30m) to correlate traces.
- Collect a sample of top P99 traces and kernel logs; we’ll also check concurrency caps and fallback routing.
- If safe, we can temporarily lift the per-tenant concurrency cap for you to relieve queueing while we investigate.

I’ll post an update in 15–20 minutes.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Customer Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0189
From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-05T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Deckridge production — quick triage notes (internal)

Onboarding notes from the Deckridge ticket — they attached client logs and queue screenshots. Early obs from telemetry:

- Model route: open-llama-13b-v1 (cpu-gpu mixed), traffic spike matched with increased KV cache misses at 08:44–08:52.
- Serving runtime: a subset of requests routed to a fallback shard where sequence-length distribution increased; that shard shows sustained GPU stalls for 300–700ms between token generation bursts.
- Autoscaler: no fast autoscale trigger fired; pool utilization at 72% but sustained queue growth.
- Concurrency cap: tenant cap is currently 250 concurrent requests; their burst pattern shows many short requests that accumulate into long sequences and fill the queue.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Backpressure from per-tenant concurrency cap + long KV cache warmups causing queue buildup.
2) Kernel stall on fallback shard amplified by weird sequence lengths (scheduling inefficiency).
3) Client-side retry pattern exacerbating the accumulation.

Immediate mitigations we can apply now (if we get customer signoff):
- Temporarily raise Deckridge cap to 400 for 30m (manual override).
- Disable the specific fallback routing rule that sends traffic to the problematic shard (route all traffic to primary pool).
- Reduce batching window to favor latency over throughput for Deckridge until tail stabilizes.

Requesting: marissa — can you check the shard kernel logs for OOMs / CUDA driver warnings between 08:40–09:00? Aditya — can you stage a cap bump + route change with a rollback plan? I’ll coordinate the bridge with the customer and capture traces.

Rachel
From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: ops@deckridge.com, alice@deckridge.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-05T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Mitigation actions taken — Deckridge production latency (RED-9482)

Hi Ops / Alice — quick status update and actions taken: we performed a short mitigation window starting 09:30 PDT. Actions (completed):

- Increased Deckridge per-tenant concurrency cap from 250 -> 400 (30m), monitor in place.
- Temporarily disabled the fallback shard routing rule for Deckridge; all traffic now bound to primary pool.
- Reduced batching window for Deckridge routes to 10ms to prioritize latency.

Immediate results: p99 dropped ~45% from the peak within 6 minutes after the change; error rate (502-ish) dropped back toward baseline. Throughput returned to ~96% of pre-incident levels.

We’ve attached the logs we pulled and a short telemetry snapshot. Next steps:
- We’ll keep the temporary cap & routing change in place for 2 hours while we run an RCA.
- We opened RED-9482 to track root cause and long-term remediation (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-9482).
- Proposed long-term fixes: smarter per-tenant burst policy, more aggressive KV prewarming for customers with heavy short-request mixes, and a routing health-check to avoid fallback on marginal shards.

Attachments: deckridge_latency_logs_20281005.zip, pipeline_snapshot_09h10.png

Would you like a short postmortem once we complete the RCA?

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Customer Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: alice@deckridge.com
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: ops@deckridge.com, support@deckridge.com
Date: 2028-10-06T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mitigation actions taken — Deckridge production latency (RED-9482)

Rachel — thanks for the quick moves and for keeping us in the loop. We saw the improvement on our side after the cap bump; checkout conversion impact is reduced and error spikes are lower.

Requests from Deckridge leadership:
- We’d like a preliminary RCA and timeline for the full root cause by EOD Monday (2028-10-08).
- Please include whether the temporary cap bump will incur overage charges or whether this is creditable — we need that discussed with our procurement.
- If there are specific SDK or client-side retry patterns that contributed, please call them out so our engineers can patch quickly.

If you want to schedule a short exec readout tomorrow, we’re available 10:00–11:30 PDT.

— Alice 
Alice Chen, CTO (Deckridge)
